# Stoic

> Robustness primitives for Swift apps (Swift 6.4, Apple platforms 27+): deadlines, retry, scopes, structured concurrency helpers, state machines, supervision, service graphs, structured errors, strict JSON and schema validation, and test tooling. Plain async functions over Swift concurrency; typed errors pass through.

Products: `Stoic` (runtime), `StoicTesting` (test clocks, faults, trait), `StoicJSON` (strict parser), `StoicSchema` (validation), `StoicHTTP` (HTTP client), `StoicMacros` (`@Schema`, `@Refined`; package trait `Macros`), `StoicSealed` (sealed files and journals; package trait `Crypto`), `StoicDownloads` (resumable verified downloads; package trait `Crypto`), `StoicTime` (dates, times, zones), `StoicXPC` (bundled XPC services, macOS).

## Time
- `withTimeout(_ duration:) { … }` / `withDeadline(_ deadline:) { … }`: cooperative; operation runs as a child task inheriting the caller's actor; result must be Sendable; error passes through. `Deadline.current` narrows, never widens.
- `abandoningAfter(_ duration:, label:, limit:) { syncWork() }`: for uncancellable blocking work; runs on Dispatch; throws `PolicyError.rejected(.deadlineExceeded)`; a label never occupies more than `limit` threads, running or abandoned; refuses with `.abandonmentLimit` once every slot is abandoned.
- `abandoningAsyncAfter(_ duration:, label:, limit:) { await uncancellableStart() }`: the async sibling for work that never checks cancellation (continuation-based starts); same ledger, limit and error; the work is cancelled at the deadline in case it does check.
- `CancellationCause.current`: `.deadline`, `.userRequested`, `.superseded`, `.siblingFailed`, `.scopeEnded`, `.supervisorStopped`, `.stateExited`.
- `Ambient.sleep(for:)`: sleep on the ambient (injectable) clock.
- `Moment.now`: when something happened, from the ambient wall clock (`Ambient.wallClock`, `CLOCK_REALTIME` by default; a test's under `withTestAmbient`). A `Duration` since the Unix epoch; `+`/`-` a `Duration`; RFC 3339 UTC text and `Codable`. Never measure with it (it jumps); never convert a clock instant into one.

## Retry
- `retry(.exponential(base: .milliseconds(200)).attempts(5)) { attempt in … }`: schedule must be bounded (`.attempts(n)`); budget per call site on by default; nested retries make one attempt; never past the deadline; rethrows the last error.
- `retry(_:attemptTimeout:) { … }`: each attempt bounded; timed-out attempts are retried.
- `attempt.idempotencyKey`: one key per operation, the same on every attempt of a `retry` (and of a `hedge`), new per `recur` run; drawn on first read from the ambient random source.
- `Schedule`: `.fixed`, `.linear`, `.exponential` (jittered, capped 5 min by default), `.fibonacci`, `.decorrelated`, `.delays([…])`; `.capped(at:)`, `.jittered()`, `.unjittered()`, `.upTo(elapsed:)`, `.union`, `.intersection`, `.andThen`, `.attempts(n)` → `BoundedSchedule` (`maximumAttempts`, `worstCase(attemptTimeout:)`).
- `Retryable` (errors classify themselves: `.retry`, `.retryAfter(d)`, `.stop`), `RetryClassifier.standard/.transientOnly/.never`, `RetryBudget.perCallSite/.named(_)/.unlimited`, `RetryNesting.singleAttempt/.allow`.
- `recur(_ schedule:) { attempt in .continue / .continueAfter(d) / .stop }` → `RecurOutcome`.

## Operations (declare facts, never numbers)
- `extension Backend { static let api = Backend.remote("api") }` (also `.system`, `.local`, `.compute`; `capacity:` is the only number); `enum API { static let user = Backend.api.readOnly("user") }` (also `.idempotent`, `.keyed`, `.notRepeatable`; `length: .long`, `ceiling:`). Declare as `static let`; one name, one kind (a conflict is `operation.backend_conflict`, which fails a test).
- `try await API.user.perform { attempt in … }`: derives the default deadline, schedule, classifier, attempt timeout, breaker, urgency-partitioned admission, budget and key from the declaration, `Urgency.current` and `Deadline.current`; runs on the caller's actor (non-Sendable captures fine); throws `OperationError<F>` (`stop: .failed(f)/.rejected(r)/.cancelled`, `outcome: .notExecuted/.executed/.unknown`, `last`, `attempts`, `idempotencyKey`). `.keyed`: send `attempt.idempotencyKey`, pass `idempotencyKey:` made with the intent (checkout opened); on `outcome == .unknown` reconcile under it, never re-ask.
- `withUrgency(.interactive) { … }` at a tap; urgency is otherwise inferred from base priority (`.background`, `.utility`, else `.userInitiated`; never `.interactive`). `op.policy(at:)` prints the derived policy for a test.
- A `perform` that gives up inside another retry's attempt settles it (never repeated); inside a `perform` on the same backend it makes one attempt. `Retryable.neverReachedBackend` lets a `.notRepeatable` operation be retried. Tests get fresh backend state under `withTestAmbient` (`Ambient.backends`). design/22.

## Concurrency
- `TaskSlot<S, F>(label:)`: `.run(for: self) { [api] in … } deliver: { @MainActor model, result in … }` (only newest delivers, on the caller's actor, which is required; the owner is held weakly and handed to `deliver`, so never capture `self` in either closure; annotate `deliver` to touch actor state), `.runExclusively(for:)`, `.cancel()`.
- `race(a, b[, c, d])` or `race([Racer { … }])`: first success; losers cancelled and awaited.
- `mapConcurrent(items, limit: n) { … }` throws `PolicyError`: `.failed(first failure)`, or `.rejected(.cancelled)` for a cancelled caller (never a shorter array); `mapConcurrentResults` returns every outcome or throws `Rejection`.
- `AsyncSemaphore(permits:label:).withPermit { … }`, `AsyncMutex(label:).withLock { … }`: FIFO, cancellation/deadline aware; throw `PolicyError`.
- `SingleFlight<K, V, F>(label:).run(key) { … }`: shared execution, refcounted cancellation.
- `Channel<T>(capacity:, overflow: .suspend/.dropOldest/.dropNewest/.reject, label:)`: bounded; `send`, `trySend`, `receive`, `finish`, `for await`.
- `Debouncer` / `Throttler`: `Policy` types (`execute { … }`, `submit(in: scope)`); a dropped call is `.rejected(.superseded)` / `.rejected(.suppressed)`, never a hang. design/20.
- `ExpiringCache.make(in: scope, ttl:, staleWindow:, maxEntries:, negativeTTL:) { key in … }`: LRU, loads single-flighted, stale-while-revalidate in the scope; a failed refresh keeps the stale value.
- `Broadcast<T>`: N subscribers, each with its own bounded buffer (`.dropOldest`, `.dropNewest`, `.suspend`).

## Scopes
- `withScope { scope in let r = try await scope.acquire { … } release: { r, exit in … } }`: LIFO release on success/failure/cancel; shielded; bounded by `exitBudget`/`finalizerTimeout`.
- `Resource(label:acquire:release:)`, `scope.onExit { exit in … }`.
- `withTaskScope { scope in scope.fork(label:) { … } }`: forks cancelled/awaited before release; a failing fork cancels the body; throws `ConcurrentFailure`.
- `withSaga { saga in try await saga.step { … } compensate: { … } }`.

## Errors
- `withContext("doing X") { … }`, `error.context("…")` → `Report` (root, frames, suppressed, `first(T.self)`); cancellation never wrapped.
- `Defect` (never retried), `PolicyError<F>` (`.rejected(Rejection)` / `.failed(F)`), `Rejection.Reason` (`.deadlineExceeded`, `.cancelled`, `.closed`, `.full`, `.abandonmentLimit`, …), `ConcurrentFailure<F>`.
- `Secret<T>` (`reveal()`), `IdempotencyKey.random()` (create outside retry, or use `attempt.idempotencyKey`).

## State machines
- `StateMachine<S, E>(initial:label:) { state, event in .to(next, timeout:) / .stay / .ignore / .invalid("why") }`; `.send(e)`; `.whileIn(state, label:, shutdownTimeout:) { sender in … }` (set up once; cancelled on exit, and the next visit's work waits for it to stop; stale events dropped; send through `sender`, never capture the machine); `.states()`; `await .shutdown()` where its owner ends.
- `StateGraph.explore(from:events:transition:)` (events `Hashable`): check `#expect(graph.isComplete)` first, then `.invalid`, `.unreachable(of:)`, `.deadEnds`; `.states`, `.mermaid`.

## Lifecycles (a stored record's states, design/27)
- Declare once: `enum Waiver: Lifecycle { static let name = "app.waiver"; typealias Principal = Someone; enum State …; enum Event …; enum Effect … (default Never); static func transition(from:on:) -> Self.Step { .to(next, effects: [...]) / .stay() / .refuse("why") / .ignore / .invalid("bug") }; static func timeout(in:) -> Self.Timeout? { .after(d, send: e) / .at(moment, send: e) }; isFinal, isRetired }`. A timeout belongs to the state, never the transition. Write `Self.Step` if the module has a type named `Step`.
- At rest, a value: `Waiver.Record.new(in:by:because:)`; `record.state()` / `.read()` apply every due timeout (an expired state is expired on every path; nothing is written). `record.applying(e, by:, because:)` → a `Change` (timed entries first, then the event's; effects with keys `IdempotencyKey.lifecycle(record:entry:position:)`) or throws `LifecycleRefusal` (`.refused(state:event:reason:)`, `.ignored`, `.invalid`, `.newerDefinition`, `.chainTooLong`). `record.written` is the state as stored: for indexes, never decisions. `because:` is required.
- Stores: `LifecycleStore` (load, history, insert, commit over a revision, `moment(for:)`); always go through `store.apply(e, to: id, by:, because:)` / `update(id) { record in … }` (retries conflicts, reports `lifecycle.*`) / `settle(id)` / `read(id)`. A server's store commits head, entries and effects in one transaction and delivers effects under `effect.key`. Tests: `InMemoryLifecycleStore` (`effects`, `conflictNextCommit(to:)`).
- On a device: `try await JournaledLifecycleStore<L, ID>.open(at:)`: a commit is one journal append; effects go to an outbox that remembers settled keys; `settleDue()` at launch and on a timer, `nextDue`, `deliverEffects { @Sendable d in … return .delivered }`, `purge(finishedBefore:)`; never reads at a moment earlier than it has seen (a clock set back cannot un-expire); records a newer build wrote are kept intact.
- Live: `StateMachine(Waiver.self, initial: .sent, perform: { effect in … })`. Check: `StateGraph.explore(Waiver.self, from: [starts], events:)`; assert `Set(graph.waitingForever) == [written list]`, and `undeclaredDeadEnds`, `finalWithExits`, `timedCycles`, `stuckTimeouts`, `retiredEntries` empty. `randomWalks(Waiver.self, from:, by:, events:) { state, entries in … }`.

## Provenance (design/28)
- At a trust boundary a value is `Claimed<T>` (anyone may make one; `map` gives a claim; prints `Claimed<T>`, never its value; `Codable` as the value). A function that needs a fact takes `Verified<T, E>` with the narrowest evidence kind `E`; only a `Minter<E>` makes one, and only code that can construct `E.Mint` makes a minter: `struct Session: PrincipalEvidence { struct Mint { fileprivate init() {} }; static let proves = "…" }`, `private let minter = Minter<Session>(Session.Mint())`, `minter.read(claim)`, `minter.verified(value, evidence)`. `claim.unverified()` is the escape (`stoic.unverified-claim`, a reason required outside tests).
- Kinds: `PrincipalEvidence` (who acts), `ContentEvidence` (who sent bytes, intact: `proof.deriving { decode($0) }` keeps it), others neither. `Verified` is `Encodable` as its value and never `Decodable`: written down, a proof is a claim. `Moment.stamped()` → `Verified<Moment, OwnClock>` (the service's own clock; a device's moment does not compile there). `Sealing.verify(Claimed(bytes), context:, keyring:)` → `Verified<[UInt8], AuthenticatedDecryption>` (not freshness).
- Permissions: `enum EditEvent: Permission { typealias Subject = EventID; typealias Principal = Someone; static let name = "events.edit" }`; `struct P: PermissionPolicy { typealias Granting = EditEvent; let name = "…"; func decide(_ who: Verified<Someone, Session>, _ subject: EventID) async throws -> PermissionDecision }` (`.allow`, `.deny(reason)`, `.unknown(.loading / .unavailable)`); `try await P().check(Claimed(id), by: me)` → `.granted(Granted<EditEvent>)` / `.denied(PermissionDenial)` / `.unknown`; never a `Bool`. On a server `check(…).granted()` throws `.denied` (`.stop`, 403) or `.unknown` (`.retry`, 503). The action takes the `Granted` in place of the id. Lifecycles: `store.apply(e, to:, by: verifiedPrincipal, because:)`. Tests: `TestProof.principal(x)`.

## App Attest (design/29)
- Proves a request came from an unmodified build of this app on genuine Apple hardware, signed by one hardware key, unaltered; never who the user is, never that the content is true. `AppAttested` is content evidence, not principal evidence.
- App: `AppAttester(account:secrets:server: .http(enrolmentClient))` (`StoicApple`; one key per account, the record kept phase by phase, one enrolment however many callers, a dead key replaced once, `availability` decided once) and `HTTPClient(base:…, authenticator: AppAttestAuthenticator(attester, signing: .unsafeMethods, ifUnsupported: .declare / .fail))` (`StoicAttestedHTTP`; every attempt signed afresh over method, authority, path, query, body digest and idempotency key; stale challenges, unknown keys, replayed counters and missing signatures repaired with one replay; revoked, invalid and `account_mismatch` end the call). The enrolment client must be another `HTTPClient`.
- Server (`StoicAttestation`, trait `Attestation`): `AppAttestGate(app: try AppID("TEAMID.bundle.id"), environment: .production, authority:, challenges: try AppAttestChallenges(keys: [secret]), ledger:, ifUnsupported: .accept / .refuse)`; `gate.challenge(.enrolment/.requests)`, `try await gate.enrol(enrolment, account:)`, `try await gate.verify(SignedRequest(method:path:query:headers:body:), account:)` → `.attested(Verified<AttestedRequest, AppAttested>, freshChallenge:)` or `.unsupported(Claimed<…>)`; refusals carry `code`, `status` and `gate.headers(for:)`. The ledger is the app's (`AppAttestLedger`: insert, compare-and-set commit, spend); `InMemoryAppAttestLedger` for tests. Pure checks: `AppAttest.verifyAttestation/verifyAssertion/verifyRequest`. Tests: `ScriptedAppAttestService` (client), `AppAttestStandIn` (real keys, a test root), and the committed vectors.

## Supervision and services
- `Supervisor(label:, strategy: .oneForOne/.oneForAll/.restForOne, intensity:, backoff:) { Child("x", restart: .permanent/.transient/.temporary, heartbeat: .init(interval:)) { heartbeat in … } }`; `try await supervisor.run()`; throws `SupervisorEscalation`.
- `ServiceGraph(label:) { Provide(key, needs: [other.any]) { services in … } stop: { value, exit in … } }`; `try await graph.run { services in … }`; `ServiceKey<T>("name")`.

## Validation
- `StoicJSON`: `JSONDocument(parsing:options:)` (duplicate keys rejected, exact numbers, positions, limits), `JSONValue`, `JSONPath`, `JSONChange.between(old, new)` (leaf-level changes; arrays are leaves) with `value.applying(change)` / `change.inverted` for a settings history and undo. `value.setting(v, at: path)` (makes the objects on the way; `JSONPathError.blocked` where a non-object is in the way), `value.removing(at: path, pruning: true)`, and `JSONPath(address: "web.routes.github.com", shape: .fields(["web": .fields(["routes": .freeKeys(.value)])]))` / `schema.path(forAddress:)` read a dotted address where a dictionary's keys may contain dots. `JSONParseOptions.allowComments = false` refuses comments in the `.jsonc` dialect.
- `StoicSchema`: `Schema.object(T.self, default: T()) { Field("key", \.prop, .double(.range(0...10)), doc:, unit:, aliases:, secret:) }`; `.decode(text) { warning in … }` throws `ValidationFailure` with every issue (path, line:col, did-you-mean) and hands warnings to the required handler (`{ _ in }` drops them, visibly); `.decodeReporting(text, options: .lenient)` returns value and issues; `Decoded.get(warnings:)`; `SchemaCoded<T>` keeps `warnings` beside `value`; wire models (no defaults) read keys exactly, `spellings: .forgiving` reads `user_id` as `userId`; `.encode(v, style: .sparse)`; `.jsonSchema()`; `Refined<R>`, `IntRange<lo, hi>`.
- `StoicSchema`, for a file people edit: `.double(.range(200...4000)).clampingToRange()` (also integers) reads a number past a bound as the nearest bound with an `out_of_range` warning (`repair`: "clamped to 4000"), in every mode; an exclusive bound still refuses. `.lossyDictionary(of: .bool, valueDoc: "…")` drops each bad entry with a `dropped_entry` warning at its own path and keeps the rest; `schema.documented("…")` sets a schema's export `description` (a dictionary's values, an array's elements). `Scroll.schema.readingNullAsEmpty()` reads `null` as `{}` silently (nothing is written back). `schema.normalizing(.rename("hyper", to: "searcher"), .mapEnum("mode", ["raw": "new"]), .custom(id:description:apply:), retired: ["old"])` (on an object schema) tidies the raw JSON on every read with no version number and no issue: a rename keeps an existing target, ops are idempotent, retired paths are no unknown keys and are not written back; `schema.normalized(json)` is the result. `schema.jsonSchema(options: JSONSchemaOptions(draft: .draft07, closesObjects: true, extraRootProperties: header.jsonSchemaProperties))` writes the editor's document (Draft-07, `additionalProperties: false` on every object whatever its unknown-key policy, the file header keys admitted); the default options are `jsonSchema()`. `.json(jsonSchema: ["$ref": "#/$defs/Graph"])` is a `Schema.json()` field whose export carries that fragment (decoding unchanged).
- `StoicMacros` (trait `Macros`; `import StoicMacros` and `StoicSchema`): `@Schema struct Settings { @Range(200...4000) @Unit("px/s") var speed: Double = 1200; @Key("api_token") @Secret var token = ""; @Length(1...253) @Count(0...8) @Unique var hosts: [String] = [] }` writes `Settings.schema` (a property with no default is required: `var id: Int` makes a missing key an issue, `var x: T?` may be missing or null, and the value is built by the memberwise init, so declare no initializers; `Date`, `URL`, `UUID`, `Data`, `Decimal` are fields, `@DateFormat(.epochSeconds)`; doc comments become `doc:`); constraint attributes `@Range @GreaterThan @LessThan @MultipleOf @Length @Pattern @Count @Unique`, markers `@Key @Secret @Unit @Aliases @Deprecated @Nullable @Ignored @PreserveUnknownKeys`; wire-model markers `@UnknownCase` (an enum case that stands for any value the client does not know: warning `unknown_case`, not an error; by hand `Schema.enumeration(T.self, unknownCase: .unknown)` or `Schema.openEnumeration(T.self, cases:, fallback:, read:, write:)`) and `@Lossy` (on an array: elements that do not decode are dropped, one `dropped_element` warning each; by hand `Schema.lossyArray(of:)`) and `@Codable` (a Codable type with no schema, read by JSONDecoder: one `invalid_value` issue on failure, export `{}`; by hand `Schema.codable(T.self, examples:)`); `@Schema(version:migrations:unknownKeys:name:)` as for `Schema.object`. On an enum: `String`/`Int` raw type is `Schema.enumeration`, cases with values are `Schema.union` (`@Schema(discriminator: "type")`, `@Key("tag")` per case). `@Refined(Double.self, .range(0.1...10)) enum Rule {}` is a `Refinement`. Without the trait write `Schema.object` by hand.

## Persistence (StoicStore)
- `AtomicFile(options: .init(keepPrevious: true)).write(bytes, to: path)` (temp, F_FULLFSYNC, rename, directory sync; checksum envelope); `.read(path, validate:)` falls back to `.previous`, quarantines corrupt files.
- `AtomicFile().replaceItem(at: dest, withItemAt: staged)`: crash-safe replace of a file or directory (`renamex_np` swap, parent synced, old removed); one volume only.
- `Journal.open(at:)`: framed, checksummed append-only log; `append` durable on return; torn tails cut on open; `compact`.
- `Outbox<Item>.open(at:codec:)`: `enqueue` (durable, assigns an `IdempotencyKey`), `deliverPending { entry in … return .delivered }` under retry; the closure returns a `DeliveryResult` (`.delivered`, `.discard(reason:)` for a refusal that is final, `.keep`), throwing leaves the entry pending; the report says `delivered` / `discarded` / `failed` / `kept`. `deliver(key) { … }` waits its turn (one delivery at a time) and returns that entry's `DeliveryOutcome`. `DeliveryPolicy(onUndecodable: .keep | .discard, expiry: .init(maxAge:))`.
- `PosixFileSystem(newFileMode: 0o600, newDirectoryMode: 0o700)`: every file and directory the store creates (journal, lock, snapshot, `AtomicFile` temporaries, outbox) has that mode from the instant it exists; pass it as the `fileSystem:` of whatever you open.
- `FileLock(path:)`: advisory `flock` on `<path>.lock`; `tryAcquire`, `acquire(timeout:)` (cancellation/deadline aware), `withLock`. `Journal.Options.crossProcessLock` and `SettingsStore.Options.crossProcessLock` refuse a second process (`.busy`).
- `LaunchGuard(path:).beginLaunch()` → `.normal` / `.safeMode(uncleanLaunches:)`; `markStable(after:)`, `markCleanExit()`.
- `FlightRecorder(path:)`: an `Instrumentation` that keeps recent events in a fixed-size file; next launch reads `previousRun` (`events`, `endedCleanly`); `markCleanExit()`, `flush()`. Private values stored as `<private>`.
- `SimulatedFileSystem` + crash-image exploration for crash-consistency tests.
- `Outbox.open(…, rememberSettled: n)`: keeps the keys of the last n entries to settle, so enqueueing one again writes nothing (`isSettled`); its snapshots are then unreadable by releases before 0.6.

## Sealed storage (StoicSealed, package trait `Crypto`)
- `Keyring.open(name:custody:ifMissing: .create/.fail)` → `.keyring`, `.created`; `ring.current`, `ring.key(id:)`, `rotate()` (persisted before returned), `retire(id:)` (crypto-shredding), `destroy()`, `reload()`. A `KeyCustody` (`load(name:)` → `nil` only when definitely absent, `store` atomic, `delete`) keeps the ring; `InMemoryKeyCustody` for tests; an app adapts `SecretStore` to it (design/24, ~20 lines). `CustodyError.unavailable` means the item may exist: never create a keyring or delete data on it.
- `Sealing.seal(plaintext, context: SealContext("purpose", ids…), key: ring.current)` / `open(sealed, context:, keyring:)`: AES-256-GCM, random nonce, header and context authenticated. `SealError`: `.tampered` (auth failed), `.torn`, `.unknownKey(id)`, `.notSealed`, `.unsupportedFormat`. Use logical ids, never paths. A key seals at most 2³² values: rotate.
- `SealedFile(keyring:)`: `write` / `read` (nil if absent) over `AtomicFile`, 0o600, previous generation sealed; `adopt(path:context:)` seals a plaintext file in place and removes `.previous`/`.tmp` plaintext (APFS does not erase old blocks).
- `SealedJournal.open(at:context:keyring:)`: `append`, `append(batch:)`, `replay()` (plaintext `records`, `snapshot`, `failures` per sequence, `report`), `compact(snapshot:rotatingKey:)` (rotate, seal the snapshot under the new key, make it durable, then retire the old keys), `SealedJournal.readOnlyReplay` for a second process. Its keyring is its own: retiring a key destroys whatever else it sealed. design/24.

## Downloads (StoicDownloads, package trait `Crypto`)
- `Downloader(client:fileSystem:policy:label:operation:)`; `try await downloader.download(Download(url, to: path, expectedSize:, digest: try .sha256(hex), fileMode: 0o644)) { progress in … }` → `DownloadResult` (`bytes`, `resumedFrom`, `requests`, `isDurable`); `download(DownloadBundle([.init(path, url, expectedSize:, digest:)], to: dir))` places a directory atomically (staging `.<name>.partial/`; whole, checking files are reused).
- Resumes by `Range` + `If-Range` (strong ETag, else Last-Modified; none and no digest: starts over); a record `<partial>.resume` vouches for the durable prefix only; the digest (`.sha256`, `.gitBlobSHA1` needs `expectedSize`; a bad hex is `ContentDigest.Invalid`) is computed while streaming, a mismatch refetches from zero `verificationAttempts` (2) times then `.digestMismatch`. Retries on `DownloadPolicy.schedule` (10 s doubling to 300 s, equal jitter, unbounded), which starts over whenever bytes arrive; 404/403 and other 4xx are final; `Retry-After` honoured. Throws `DownloadError` or `CancellationError` (never a failure; partial kept unless `keepsPartialOnCancel: false`; a deadline is `.deadlineExceeded` and keeps it). Declare the operation `length: .long` and set a deadline (design/22's default is 90 s at `.userInitiated`). `fileMode` defaults to `0o600`. Events `download.*`, none with a query string. Tests: `ScriptedTransport` `.serving(Resource(bytes, etag:), fault: .cut(after:))`, `SimulatedFileSystem`. design/23.

## Settings (StoicSettings)
- `SettingsStore.open(at:schema:)`: `value` (Observable), `try update { $0.x = … }` (validated against the schema, written atomically, then published; throws `.invalid(issues)`, `.newerFormat`, `.storage`), `issues` (what the load repaired/migrated), `source` (`.file`, `.previousGeneration`, `.defaults(.missing/.unusable)`, `.newerFormat`). Never fails because of file contents; a newer app's file is read-only.
- A file a person edits (`format: .handEdited`, `options: .init(handEdited: HandEditedOptions(fileHeader: ["$schema": "x.json"]))`): never quarantined, renamed or overwritten when it is not JSON, not UTF-8 or unreadable: load keeps the last good value (defaults the first time) and sets `fileProblem` (`.unparsable(issues)` with `Issue.source` line and column, `.unreadable(error)`); `update` throws `.fileUnusable`. Every issue carries `source`, the range in the text (coarse after a migration). Writes are sparse and byte-stable (`.canonical`: declared order, then unknown keys alphabetical, header first, final newline). `update` reads the file again under `<path>.lock` (`.busy` if held now); `try await coordinatedUpdate { … }` waits up to `lockTimeout` (2 s). `reload()` re-reads (nothing happens for a file unchanged since the store last saw it); `try settings.watch(debounce:)` reloads when the file changes (directory watch: kqueue / inotify; a burst is one reload on the ambient clock; the store's own writes find nothing changed). `FileSystem.watchFile(at:handler:)` is the primitive. `layout: .canonical(order: KeyOrder(root: ["lode", "app"], nested: [["web"]: ["routes"]]))` puts the listed keys first at the document and at the objects named (then declared fields, then alphabetical; array elements share the array's path), also over `Schema.json()`; the header is never part of the value the schema reads. `HandEditedOptions(comments: .refused)` makes a comment a `fileProblem` at its line and column (default `.allowed`: an update drops comments). The dialect of the file (comments, trailing commas, a BOM, repeated keys, limits) is the table on `HandEditedOptions`; `parseOptions` is it as `JSONParseOptions`. A key said twice is read `.lastWins` by default WITH a `repeated_key` warning in `issues` carrying both places (the next update writes only the last; `duplicateKeys: .refused` makes it a `fileProblem`). `Schema.jsonObject()` is `Schema.json()` for a document whose top level must be an object (anything else is a `type_mismatch` problem). `fileProblem.isNotUTF8` / `.parseCode` answer why the text could not be read. `try settings.blockingUpdate(waitingUpTo: .seconds(2)) { … }` is the synchronous update that waits for the lock by BLOCKING THE THREAD (real time, 25 ms polls; not on the main actor; use `coordinatedUpdate` where you can `await`). `try settings.update(source: "settings window") { … }` (also `coordinatedUpdate(source:)`, `blockingUpdate(source:)`) puts the tag on `SettingsChange.source`. `try settings.blockingMaterialize(waitingUpTo:)` and `blockingReplaceUnusableFile(with:keepingCopyAt:waitingUpTo:source:)` are the two whole-file writes for a synchronous caller that waits for the lock by BLOCKING THE THREAD (`.zero` tries once). `try settings.materialize()` writes the sparse file with the header if there is none (never touches one that is there); `try settings.replaceUnusableFile(with: Prefs(), keepingCopyAt: nil)` is the reset for a file that cannot be read: it re-reads under the lock, replaces only a still-unusable file, copies the person's bytes to `<path>.broken-N` (checked, never over a file) first, and returns the copy's path. `for await change in settings.changes(buffering: 64)` yields `SettingsChange(old:, new:, cause: .update / .reload / .reset)` once per change of the value, in commit order (the store's own write that the watcher re-reads is not a second change; an update that finds the file moved is a `.reload` change then its own `.update`); the buffer is bounded, the oldest are dropped and `settings.change_dropped` says so. `for await change in settings.problems()` yields `SettingsProblemChange(old:, new:, cause:)` (`began` / `ended`: the file stopped parsing / parses again) once per change of `fileProblem`, beside `changes()` and not in it, with the same bound. Events: `settings.unparsed`, `settings.reloaded`, `settings.busy`, `settings.update_refused`, `settings.materialized`, `settings.replaced`, `settings.change_dropped`.

## XPC services (StoicXPC, macOS)
- Declare methods once in a module the app and the service both import: `static let respond = XPCMethod<Generate, String, ModelsFailure>(Backend.models.notRepeatable("respond", length: .long), ifStuck: .endService(after: .seconds(20)))`. Request, reply and failure are `Codable`; a method that cannot fail says `Never`; `XPCEmpty` for nothing. Bulk data as `Data` (a large `[Float]` through XPC's `Codable` is ~1000× slower).
- App: `let models = XPCPeer(service: "com.example.app.models", build: Build.id)` (one per service per process; `build` is a compiled-in value both sides share). `try await models.call(ModelsAPI.respond, request)` is a `perform` of the method's operation (design/22) and throws `OperationError<XPCCallError<Failure>>`: `.failed(Failure)`, `.lost(afterSending:)` (the run ended on its own), `.ended(afterSending:)` (the app ended it: not counted by the breaker), `.cancelled(afterSending:)`, `.notRunning` (`ifRunning: true`, starts nothing), `.buildMismatch`, `.unavailable(.noSession/.noHandshake/.wedged/.shutDown)`, `.refused` (not run), `.protocolViolation` (a bad reply). `models.end(reason:)` → `.exited / .killed / .wedged`; `models.run` is the live `XPCRun`; `shutdown()`.
- Service: `let host = XPCHost(build: Build.id, policy: XPCHostPolicy(idleExit: .seconds(30)))`; `host.handle(ModelsAPI.respond) { request, context throws(ModelsFailure) in … }` (own task, under the caller's remaining deadline, cancelled when the caller cancels); `host.hold("model")` / `release` keep an idle service alive; `host.run()` never returns. The watchdog exits a service whose handler ignores cancellation past budget + `watchdogGrace` (the only way a wedged service ends in a sandbox).
- Tests: `XPCSimulatedService { makeHost() }` as the peer's `transport:` (`crash(sessionsEndFirst:)`, `dropSessions()`, `exitLag`, `launchDelay`, `permitsKill`, `refusesConnections`, `runs`, `exits`), on a `TestClock`. Events `xpc.*`. design/25.

## HTTP (StoicHTTP)
- `HTTPClient(base:policy:transport:headers:)`: `try await api.send(.get("/users/42"), decoding: User.schema)`, `api.send(.post("/orders", json: v), idempotencyKey: key)` → `HTTPResponse`. Per host, in order: caller's deadline, retry, breaker, bulkhead, attempt timeout, transport. Only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/PUT/DELETE, or POST/PATCH with an `IdempotencyKey` (sent as `Idempotency-Key`, same on every attempt), are retried; `Retry-After` honoured, capped, never past the deadline; identical GETs in flight share one request.
- `HTTPPolicy.singleAttempt` (one attempt, no breaker, 10 s kept: for callers that retry elsewhere, such as an outbox; `keyedConflictIsInProgress = false` makes a keyed 409 final), `HTTPPolicy.standard` (10 s attempt, 3 attempts, 8 in flight per host, 10 MB, 10 redirects), `HTTPError` (`.status`, `.transport`, `.timedOut(attempt:)`, `.responseTooLarge`, `.decoding(ValidationFailure)`, `.rejected(Rejection)`, `.redirectRefused(reason, status:, location:)`; each says `attempts`); cancellation is `CancellationError`.
- Redirects are followed by the client, not the transport (`HTTPPolicy.maxRedirects`, default 10): each hop through its own host's policies, under the caller's deadline, not a retry. Never `https` → `http` (`.redirectRefused(.downgrade)`). Default headers go only to the base URL's origin (scheme, host, port); once a redirect changes origin only `Accept`-style headers go along (no credentials, custom headers or idempotency key). 301/302 `POST` and 303 become `GET` without the body; 307/308 keep method and body.
- Tests: `ScriptedTransport().on(.get("/x"), respond: [.status(503), .json("{}")])` (also `.failure(code)`, `.hang`, `.oversized(n)`, `.after(delay)` on the ambient clock); records `requests` with headers. `URLSessionTransport` is the real one.

- `HTTPOverrides` per `send` (timeout, schedule, coalesce, `bypassBreaker`, `retryOnResponse`); `HTTPClient(reauthenticate:)` replays once after a 401 (single-flighted); `HTTPPolicy.rateLimit` per-host token bucket.

## Foundation (StoicFoundation)
- Linking it makes `URLError`, `POSIXError` and `CocoaError` `Retryable`: transient network and POSIX failures retry, a bad URL, a rejected certificate or a full disk stop. `StoicApple` and `StoicHTTP` link it. HTTP status semantics (`HTTPRetry`, `HTTPStatusError`) are in `StoicHTTP`.

## Apple (StoicApple)
- `PathMonitor` (`SystemPathMonitor`, `FakePathMonitor`): `stablePaths(settle:)`, `waitUntilReachable(until:)`.
- `BackgroundJob`: BGTask work under the system's expiration (`.systemExpiring`), completed once, rescheduled; `drainingOutbox`.
- `SecretStore` (`KeychainSecretStore`, `InMemorySecretStore`): errors never contain the key's value.

## Observability
- `withSpan("name", [attributes]) { … }`: task-local `Span.current`, parent ids, duration on the ambient clock, cancellation is a status not an error; free when no sink wants debug events.
- `Ambient.instrumentation` (default OSLog), `Event` (stable names in `EventCatalog`), `RecordingInstrumentation`.

## Testing
- `TestClock` (`advance(by:)`, `waitForSleepers(count:)`), `ImmediateClock` (records sleeps; not for timeouts), `withTestAmbient(clock:seed:events:)`, `@Test(.stoic(seed:))`, `FaultInjector`, `TestGate`; `expectTrace(events, """…""")` asserts the exact decisions a scenario made (golden trace).
- `simulate(seeds: 0..<500) { sim in … }`: deterministic simulation. A seed picks every interleaving, time is virtual (`sim.clock` advances when everything sleeps), failures name the seed (`simulate(seed: 137)` replays it), deadlocks are `stalled` with the stuck tasks, livelocks hit `virtualTimeLimit`. Fault points inside Stoic's primitives (slow finalizers, late retries, delayed sends) fire under simulation by seed (`faults: .standard`; `.none` to turn off); `faultsFired` lists them. The seed also picks the schedule (uniform, or PCT at depth 2 to 4, for bugs that need one task to run far ahead) and on half the seeds lets timers fire while work is still runnable; `schedule:` forces one and `Simulated.schedule` names it. The main actor, app-started `Task {}`, Dispatch and real I/O are outside it.

## Dates and zones (StoicTime)
- Pick the type by the question: `Moment` (when did it happen), `PlainDate` (which day: birthdays, due dates), `PlainTime`, `PlainDateTime` (a wall reading, no zone), `ZonedDateTime` (when is it planned, and where), `Period` (calendar days/months/years; not a `Duration`), `TimeZoneID` (IANA name). Never `Date()`, a local-time string with no zone, or a future event stored in UTC.
- `try PlainDate(2027, 3, 14)` (30 February throws `TimeError.invalid`), `try PlainDate.today(in: zone)` (no ambient zone: say `event.zone` or `.device`), `date.adding(.months(1), overflow: .constrain/.reject)`, `period(to:)`, `days(to:)`, `age(on:leapDayBirthday: .marchFirst/.februaryLast)`.
- `try ZonedDateTime(date, time, in: "America/New_York", resolving: .compatible/.earlier/.later/.reject)`: keeps `local` and `zone` (the truth) and the derived `moment` (sort and filter on it); `resolution` is `.exact`, `.gap(shiftedBy:)`, `.overlap(chose:)` or `.decoded`. `try moment.in(zone)`. After a rules change: `try value.isStale()` / `try value.refreshed()` (by the policy the value was made with; future values only; past ones are final). `var sweep = ZoneRulesSweep()` (persist it): `try await sweep.run(values: { … }) { moved in … }` runs once per rules version.
- Text forms (and `Codable`): RFC 3339 `Moment`, `2027-03-14`, `09:00:30.5`, `2027-03-14T09:00`, RFC 9557 `2027-03-14T09:00:00-04:00[America/New_York]`, ISO 8601 `P1M`; `init(parsing:)` throws with the reason; schema leaves `.moment`, `.plainDate`, `.plainTime`, `.plainDateTime`, `.zonedDateTime`, `.period`, `.timeZoneID`. Foundation: `Moment(date)`, `moment.date`, `TimeZone(id)`.
- Tests: `withTestAmbient(clock:)` puts `Moment.now` at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, moving with `advance`; `clock.jumpWallClock(by:)` moves only the wall clock. `let rules = ScriptedZoneRules(version: "2026a", deviceZone: …)`, `rules.define(zone, offset:, transitions:)`, change `rules.version`; `withZoneRules(rules.rules) { … }`. Events `time.resolved_in_gap`, `time.zone_rules_changed`. design/26.

## Lint (StoicLint plugin, `Lint` trait)
- Fails the build on: blocking in async code, `@unchecked Sendable`, `nonisolated(unsafe)`, `@preconcurrency`, `try!`, a discarded `try?`, `Task.detached`, `asyncAfter`, unbounded `AsyncStream`, `Task.sleep` without a clock, a `catch` that swallows cancellation or (catch-all, empty or print-only) errors, `IdempotencyKey.random()` inside `retry`, a hand-rolled retry or keep-alive loop (catch + sleep), `addTask` once per element of a collection, unsafe continuations, `Date()` / `Date.now` / `Calendar.current` / `TimeZone.current` (use `Moment.now`, `PlainDate.today(in:)`, `TimeZoneID.device`). Justify one site with `// stoic:allow(<rule>): <why>`; adopt gradually with a baseline (design/13).
